long-title: We know more about the health of some groups of people than others (reflecting inequality and data gaps)
icon: bar chart, diagram, data, analysis, comparison.svg

sections.long-title: What is the level being targeted?

content.choice-subtitle: Things that happen between individuals, like one-to-one support or care

content.long-title: Who should be involved?
content: People who are at risk or outside everyday society (e.g. homeless people)
Victims of domestic violence
People in care or who have left care
People who have been in the armed forces
People with dementia
People with learning or development disabilities
People who receive or give unpaid care
People who are refugees
People who are seeking asylum
People who entered the country illegally
People who do not turn up for appointments
The general public

content.long-title: What are the causes of the problem?
content: People don’t have enough money to access care or resources
People don’t feel part of society and may be socially excluded
People can’t speak English, making communication and understanding difficult
People are receiving or giving unfunded care, which limits support and visibility
People are refugees and may face barriers to accessing health services
People find it hard to get care because of complex systems or discrimination
People have learning or developmental needs that make health information harder to understand
People do not have a home address, which prevents registration and follow-up

content.long-title: What would help to solve the problem?
content: People who provide care being friendly and welcoming
Having specialist trusted link workers

content.long-title: What actions are involved in doing something about this?
content: Working with people who receive services
Telling people what they are entitled to
Helping people claim what they are entitled to
Building trust
Teaching people how to use the systems
Supporting people to become more active in their own health

content.long-title: What do we expect to come out of these actions?
content: More people will be included in datasets

content.long-title: How will we know things have changed?
content: Being able to measure health of more people (using tools like the EQ5D)
Being able to measure wellbeing of more people (using tools like the Edinburgh wellbeing scale)
Being able to describe levels of illness in more people

content.choice-subtitle: Things that happen in organisations or communities, like teamwork or service coordination
content.long-title: What would help?
Who should be involved?
content: Charities
Organisations that provide services
Organisations that teach English

content.long-title: What are the causes of the problem?
content: Organisations not  working together
Lack of services teaching English
Lack of effective information gathering

content.long-title: What would help to solve the problem?
content: People and teams who provide services working together
Working with people who teach English
Developing health information in other languages
Having services that people can use

content.long-title: What actions are involved in doing something about this?
content: Mapping out the teams and organisations that provide services
Working with people who provide services
Using information we already have
Setting goals to improve that data that is gathered

content.long-title: How will we deliver these actions?
content: Improve systems
Develop better datasets
Develop data systems that talk to each other

content.long-title: What do we expect to come out of these actions?
content: Data sets will be improved

content.long-title: How will we know things have changed?
content: Higher number (and proportion) of previously excluded people on databases

content.choice-subtitle: Big system-wide things, like national policies or data systems
content.long-title: What would help?
Who should be involved?
content: People/organisations who look after health and social care data

content.long-title: What are the causes of the problem?
content: Data is not effectively gathered or managed

content.long-title: What would help to solve the problem?
content: Organisations having good policies and systems in place e.g. for gathering and looking at data

content.long-title: What actions are involved in doing something about this?
content: Setting goals to improve the data that is gathered

content.long-title: How will we deliver these actions?
content: Develop a central database of all patients
